description: Executable evidence for identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 8: published test signing material is refused on every formal verification path by its canonical public-key fingerprint, renaming and re-encoding do not evade it, the three reserved-identifier rules are matched independently by typed-identifier semantics, unregistered material is still verified normally, and the only execution exemption is an isolated conformance harness.

decision_points.requirement: Material whose private key is published is refused even when its signature verifies and every other precondition holds.
The fingerprint covers algorithm-defined key bytes, so a different kid, DID or encoding of the same public key is still refused.
The refusal applies to proof-of-possession admission as well as to DID authority calls, from the one registry.
Material that is not registered is still verified by the ordinary identity and trust rules.
A refusal writes nothing to caches or binding stores and does not degrade into another evidence class, a limited-trust pin or a retryable unavailability.
Only an isolated conformance harness may execute the material; the formal verification API exposes no switch onto the test trust path.
A reserved DID is matched by method and SCID segment after typed parsing, independently of the key and of the fragment.
A reserved verification-method fragment is matched on its own, so rehosting it under a deployment DID does not evade the refusal.
A reserved trust domain is matched as the value of its typed identifier at trust admission, before anything signed under it becomes an authorization basis.
Matching never degrades into DNS suffix guessing or into inferring reservation from the words test, fixture, did:key or example.
Each refusal is attributable to exactly one rule, and matching one rule does not imply the others.

cases.name: a_published_fixture_key_is_refused_although_its_signature_verifies
cases.given: an event proof signed by the registered Ed25519 conformance key, presented on a DID authority call whose every other precondition holds: the DID resolves, the verification method is present in the resolved document, the method head and version pin match, and the freshness profile is satisfied
cases.action: verify the proof and admit the key as the authorization basis
cases.observed: the verification outcome and the authorization basis the call site ends up holding
assertions: the signature verifies cryptographically and the call is refused anyway, because the private key is published
the refusal is decided by the canonical public-key fingerprint, not by the signature result
no verification result is produced for the material, so nothing downstream can treat it as an authorization basis
the case satisfies every other identity and trust precondition, so the refusal cannot be explained by an independently invalid DID

cases.name: the_same_key_under_a_different_kid_and_did_is_refused
cases.given: the registered Ed25519 conformance public key republished under a freshly minted deployment DID and an unrelated verification-method fragment, with a DID document that resolves and validates
cases.action: verify a proof signed by that key
assertions: renaming the key id and rehosting the key under another DID does not change the fingerprint, so the refusal is unchanged
neither reserved-identifier rule fires here: the DID and the fragment are both ordinary, and the published-material rule alone decides
an implementation that matched on the DID or the kid instead of the key material would admit this case, which is the failure this case exists to catch

cases.name: the_same_key_re_encoded_is_refused
cases.given: the registered Ed25519 conformance public key carried once as a JWK with reordered members, once as a multibase multicodec value and once as a PEM SubjectPublicKeyInfo
cases.action: verify a proof against each encoding in turn
cases.observed: the fingerprint computed for each encoding and the verification outcome
assertions: all three encodings produce the identical fingerprint, because the fingerprint covers the algorithm-defined key bytes and not the transport text
all three are refused
an implementation that hashed the JWK text would produce three different fingerprints and admit at least two of these, which is the failure this case exists to catch

cases.name: published_p256_and_mldsa_material_are_refused_under_their_own_encodings
cases.given: the registered P-256 conformance key presented as a SEC1 uncompressed point and the registered ML-DSA-65 conformance key presented as its FIPS 204 public key
cases.action: verify a proof signed by each
cases.observed: the verification outcome for each algorithm
assertions: each algorithm uses its own canonical public-key encoding for the fingerprint
both are refused
the post-quantum key is refused on the same rule as the classical keys, so a post-quantum verification path is not an unguarded second door

cases.name: the_rfc8032_test_key_is_refused_on_the_possession_path
cases.given: a WebSocket DPoP proof whose confirmation key is the registered RFC 8032 TEST 1 key, with a well-formed protected header, a live nonce and an unexpired issue time
cases.action: verify the proof of possession and bind the connection
assertions: the rule applies to proof-of-possession admission, not only to DID authority calls
the proof is syntactically perfect and is still refused
one registry serves every formal verification path, so closing one path does not require a second list

cases.name: unlisted_material_is_still_verified_normally
cases.given: a freshly generated Ed25519 key that is not registered, presented with the same document shape, freshness and proof structure as the first case
cases.observed: the verification outcome and the resulting verification result
assertions: the material is admitted by the ordinary identity and trust rules
no presumption of suspicion attaches to material merely because it is not registered
an implementation that refused everything would pass the negative cases and fail here, which is why this case is required

cases.name: a_refusal_leaves_no_cached_state_and_no_weaker_fallback
cases.given: a call site holding a resolution cache, a verified-binding store and more than one evidence class it could use
cases.action: present the registered Ed25519 conformance key, then retry the same call through every other evidence class
cases.observed: the cache and binding store contents after the refusal, and the outcome of each retry
assertions: nothing about the refused material is written to the resolution cache, the verified-binding store or any accepted auth-state
an already cached entry for that material is dropped rather than marked stale
no other evidence class admits it, and it is not degraded to a limited-trust pin
the refusal is not reported as a transient unavailability that a retry could clear

cases.name: an_isolated_harness_may_execute_the_material_and_the_formal_api_exposes_no_switch
cases.given: the conformance fixture runner executing inside the isolated harness context, and the same build's formal verification API
cases.action: run the signature fixtures in the harness, then enumerate every configuration key, feature flag and environment variable the formal verification API reads
cases.observed: the harness execution result and the configuration surface of the formal API
assertions: the harness verifies the published material, which is what the fixtures are published for
the formal verification API exposes no configuration key, feature flag, environment variable or runtime switch that routes it onto the test trust path
the exemption is carried by the separate harness execution context, never by a mode of the formal API

cases.name: a_reserved_did_scid_is_refused_by_the_did_rule_alone
cases.given: a did:webvh whose SCID segment is a registered conformance prefix, holding an unregistered freshly generated key and an otherwise valid document
cases.action: run a DID authority call against it
cases.observed: which reserved-identifier rule decided the refusal
assertions: the DID is split into method and method-specific id before the SCID segment is compared, so the decision is not a substring scan of the whole string
the key material is unregistered, so the published-material rule cannot be what refused it
the verification-method fragment is ordinary, so the key-id rule cannot be what refused it

cases.name: a_reserved_key_id_under_a_deployment_did_is_refused_by_the_key_id_rule_alone
cases.given: an ordinary deployment did:webvh holding an unregistered key whose verification-method fragment carries the registered conformance suffix
cases.action: select that verification method and verify a proof
cases.observed: which reserved-identifier rule decided the refusal
assertions: the fragment is matched on its own, so a fixture key id rehosted under a deployment DID is still refused
the DID rule does not fire, because the SCID segment is ordinary
the published-material rule does not fire, because the key is unregistered

cases.name: a_reserved_trust_domain_is_refused_at_trust_admission
cases.given: a trust admission request carrying an ak:trust_domain typed identifier whose value is a registered conformance trust domain, with every other admission precondition satisfied
cases.action: admit the trust domain into the local trust surface
cases.observed: the trust surface after the admission attempt
assertions: the value is taken from the typed identifier before it is compared, not matched against the raw request text
the trust domain is not written into the local trust surface
the refusal happens at admission, before anything signed under that domain can become an authorization basis

cases.name: a_deployment_domain_that_merely_shares_a_tail_is_not_refused
cases.given: trust admission requests for a registered conformance value extended by a further label, and for a real domain whose spelling merely resembles a reserved label
cases.observed: the admission outcome for each value
assertions: a value whose rightmost label is not a reserved top label and whose full value is not registered is admitted
matching is by label sequence and exact registered value, never by DNS suffix guessing over the string
an implementation that treated the registered values as string suffixes would refuse both of these, which is the failure this case exists to catch

cases.name: the_word_fixture_alone_reserves_nothing
cases.given: a deployment DID, a verification-method fragment that contains but does not end with the reserved suffix, and a trust domain containing the word example as part of a longer label
cases.action: verify a proof and admit the trust domain
assertions: no identifier is reserved because it contains the words test, fixture, did:key or example
only the registered naming rules reserve anything, and each is matched by its own typed-identifier semantics
an implementation that scanned for those words would refuse legitimate deployment material

cases.name: matching_one_rule_does_not_imply_the_others
cases.given: the three refusal cases above, each of which trips exactly one rule
cases.action: record, for each case, which of the three rules matched
cases.observed: the per-rule match vector for each case
assertions: each refusal is attributable to exactly one rule
the three rules are evaluated independently, so an implementation cannot satisfy the obligation with a single combined heuristic
a fragment such as runtime-1 under a reserved DID is refused by the DID rule while the key-id rule does not match it
